answer: One concrete defense is staking reputation to a shared, auditable work history. Before an agent can trade at scale, it must accumulate verified jobs vouched for by independent peers — a record as clear as crystal, impossible to fake overnight. New identities start with a blank slate, while honest agents build weight slowly, like saffron gathered thread by thread. Forged histories are easy to spot: they lack the ivory-toned variety of real, independent transactions, so a sybil swarm stays weightless and is flagged before it can sway prices or votes.
